div.head: Close Game at Earlestown.
div.p: Close Game at Earlestown.
Crosfield's second elevni played Earlestown, at Earlystown. This is a new, club und was their first att-zupt'at-.zzrious hoetc‘y.

took the fiald with only ten men. The opening stages were contested vigorously, and the visitors opened their score with a smart goal by Clarke. This success was soon increased, Swinton putting a nice shot in, the goalkeeper only clearing to see Worthington, who had followed up, put the ball in the net. After a smart passing bout Worthington again scored, and half-time arrived with the visitors leading by three goals.

The second half saw the home- team to Getter advantage, and after some good combination they reduced the lead. From the bully-off the home team again took the upper hand, but were kept in check by the visitors' backs. The visitors now made a splendid effort, but the full-back cleared at the expense of a corner and nothing resulted, the home forwards -taking the ball down the field and the centre-forward beat the goalkeeper With a low shot. The home forwards kept to the visitors' half, but were held in check by the resolute defence, no further scoring bik- ing place. Result: Crosfield's, three goals; Earlestown, two. STOCKTON HEATH v. CHORLTON.

Stockton Heath were at home to Chorlton on Saturday. From the bully Baxter ran right through and was unlucky with his shot, which struck the upright and went behind. From the "25 " the home forwards again got into the visitors' circle, Richardson, with an open goal, shooting wide. The home . team continued to pfe-ss, and plaT was kept in the visitors' half for the first 15 minutes. A free hit brought relief, and the right wing made a fine run to near the corner flag, when he passed across, for Parry to open 6e-scoring with a fast high shot, which gave the goalkeeper no-chance. On restarting Baxter again went right through and made no mistake this time, oDening. the scoring for Stockton Heath. after 25'aliciFs' play. The home team continued to press, the visiting defence playing up strongly, the goal- keeper bringing off several fine saves. Half- time: Stockton Heath, one goal; 'llorlton, one goal.

The second half opened strong. Baxter, get- ting possession from the bully, passed out to Richardson, who, after a fine run, scOred' with a -fine low gigot. Stockton Heath continued to press, but could do nothing in the circle. With 15" minutes- to play Baxter scored: a third for Stockton Heath. The visitors nOW had a short spell Of attacking,- but the strong bitting of the home hails soon transferred play to the other end. The home team played up strongly for the last few minutes, but could not score. For the visitors, the goalkeeper gave a fine exhibition, his judgment and clearing being very fine. Stockton Heath played well all round, though the forwards Were very wild and erratic in the circle. Partridge, who was back in his old position, played a fine game. A feature of the game was the large -number of corners that were conceded, and not one was scored from.. Stockton Heath are away to Timperley to-day.

div.head: DR. JOSEPH ON AMBULANCE WORK,
div.p: DR. JOSEPH ON AMBULANCE WORK,

The DEPUTY MAYOR proposed the toast of "The Warrington Corps of the St. John Ambulance Brigade." „In regard to the housing question, he thought the Corporation could never take the part properly of private enterprisers. They could step in- so far as health was concerned, but they could never do it for profit, as they hoped private enterprisers could do it. He had witnessed the examinations of the St. John Am- bulance Corps at the drill hall in the Police Station, and he had been particularly struck with the cool alertness, intelligent action and presence of mind shown by the men. He had also been struck by the fact that the members of the corps were so self-denying as to give their time as well as their intelligence•to that noble work, which was done for the benefit of the community. In regard to "first aid," he would like to say that the medical men were not jealous, but liked to assist skilled first aid. .(Hear, hear.); After euluising on the splendid work done by the brigade to the townspeople, and especially the works, Councillor Joseph said he was pleased to congratulate the corps on winning the Crosfield Shield and the A shton-in- Makerfield Shield, and he only hoped that suc- cess was a forerunner of similar honours in the future.

div.head: MEDICAL MEN AND THE CORPS.
div.p: MEDICAL MEN AND THE CORPS.

In reply, Dr. LAW referred to the brigade as a noble body of men. The medical men, he said, did not look on the brigade with the eye of jealousy, but they had the greatest admiration for the men Who were associated with that noble The men gave their services benefit of their fellows, and exer- cisedsimorganisation.f or th a considerable amount of self-denial. He hoped the townspeople would give the brigade all the support they could. Being connected with the Infirmary, he noticed the large amount of good work done by the members of the bri- gade. They gave every encouragement to the work. They were proud of the brigade for haV- ing associated itself with the Voluntary Aid Detachment. They were showing that they were ready to meet any invasion which might be coming. (Applause.)

div.head: AMBULANCE INSTRUCTION.
div.p: AMBULANCE INSTRUCTION.

Who Should Pay For It—Town or Nation? Proposing the toast "Our Guests,' Capt. WARING said he was proud to command- such a body of men. The men did a noble and excel- lent work. They had got so many works in the town, and with the exception of Crosfield's, Rylands Bros.',. Pearson and Knowles', the L. and N.-W. Railway and C.L.C. Railway, they had not got a single man connected with the works. He did not know what the insurance companies were thinking about. (Laughter.) The doctors were not allowed now to give lec- tures free, as they had hitherto kindly done, and an effort was being made to get the Education Committee to help in the matter. The members of the brigade were ever willing to give all the assistance they could. He coupled with the toast Mr. Parr, Mr. Fulton Smith, and the Chief Constable.

Mr. R. C. PARR; as treasurer of the Hospital, said he was sure, from the treasurer's point of view, that Association ought to be encouraged. because the first aid rendered .saved considerable trouble on many occasions.

- Mr. FULTON-SMITH said. the brigade rendered disinterested services to the community. They should an 'support the brigade to .the best of their ability. The CHIEF CONSTABLE said he thought the bri- gade ought to be nationally assisted. Supt. Baldry- was a most excellent instructor, and gave the men much good advice. The brigade helped the police on many occasions, notably, when the . King visited Warringtozi, and the 'Ake .were more than. grateful .for such . ser- vices. (Applause.)
Private PRICE proposed a vote of thanks to Capt. Waring and the officers for providing that function.
This was heartily carried.

Dr. AfANSON proposed a vote of thanks to the Chairman, and said Dr. Adams had been longer connected with the brigade than any other medical man in Warrington. The British Medical Association, whose recent action respect- ing ambulance lectures had been criticised :had no desire to hamper the work of the brigade. There was the same tendency in the' history of all voluntary associations. The Army, now a State institution, was Once Maintained by a voluntary levy on landed gentry, -and the Navy was very much in the same position, as vessels' owned by" shipowners were, formerly seized by the Government. He thought the veto with regard to the Ambulance Brigade was only temporary, and that better methods would be adopted for the purpose of obtaining recruits. At any rate he hoped -arrangements would be made for the continuance of lectures. (Applause.)
- - The toast was received with -ninsical honours cheers being given both' for the Doctor and Mrs Adams. -

Dr. ADAMS, in replY, explained that he had had charge of two or three classes, but he did not know how they would get on financially with the others which were talked about, in view of the resolution which had been passed to the effect that medical men had to extract the cur- rent coin of the realm in return for their pro- fessional services. But difficulties were made to be overcome. He proposed a hearty vote of thanks to the artistes ,and pianists', which Mr. WILLIAMSON seconded. Mr. SPANN supported.
Mr. GROI7NDS'
• Senior Sergeant- A. FELL proposed a vote of thanks to Supt. Baldry, -First Officer Williamson and Second Officer Spann. _
Supt. B.U.DRY suitably replied.

div.head: SUCCESSFUL FUSION.
div.p: SUCCESSFUL FUSION.
Warrington Savings Bank has a Prosperous Year.
RUNCORN AMALGAMATION.

The recent amalgamation of the Warrington Savings Bank with the Runcorn and District Savings Bank has proved successful. This was what one gathered at the annual meeting of the trustees and managers of the Warrington, Run- corn and District Savings Bank, held in Butter- market-street, Warrington, on Tuesday. Mr. C. Jackson Holmes, vice-chairman, presided. The 96th annual report presented by the com- mittee stated: The amalgamation of the Run- corn Savings Bank with this Bank, as from the 21st November, 1913. • By the amalgamation the Runcorn Savings Bank obtained increased facilities for thrift for its depositors by opening a special investment department, and thus add- ing to its usefulness. The Amalgamated Bank would also be enabled to extend the advantageg of the investment department overB lunch larger area. The increase in the number ef accounts, viz., 320, and in the amount One to depositors, viz., .t 10,244 us. 6d., must be consid- ered very satisfactory. During the year 894 accounts had been opened or renewed in the ordinary department, and 628 closed, whilst in the investment department 100 accounts were opened or renewed and 46 ciosed, showing an increase of 320 f-ir the yea!, and making a grand total of 17,427 open accounts in the two departments. The year had been a record one, in the number of transactions, viz., 34,955, of which 23,544 were deposits, and 11,411 TrAyments, an increase over last year of 1,351. There was an increase of £10,244 us. fal. in the amormt standing to the credit of the depositors, who had now due to them £483,294 4s. 5d., an increase of over £llB,OOO in the last ten years. The school banks now numbered 30, and had standing to their credit the large amount of £1,684 3s. 9d.

div.head: Funds of Half a Million.
div.p: Funds of Half a Million.

Mr. C. JACKSON HOLMES moved the. adoption of the statements of accounts, and said there was an increase due to depositors of £10,244, who had now due to them £483,294. The funds of the Bank totalled nearly half a million pounds. The . branches at Earlestown and Bank Quay had done well, and, notwithstanding the t 3 weeks' coal strike at Haydock, the amount standing to the credit of the Earlestown deposi. tors had increased by over £6OO. &Applause.) Home safes continued to be popular, although he would, however, like to see more inquired for. The number of school banks had not in- creased, but as they had 30 of these on their books, which had introduced' 46 new accounts during the year, he supposed they could not expect to get many more until some new schools were built. The thanks of the community %- are due to those teachers who took an interest in the work and trained their scholars to look after their pennies. Thrifty habits a(quired in youth did much to build up a r rosperous future, and should unquestionably form n part of the education of every child. Facilities were given in nearly every elem.-mtaty school for saving by means of penny banks, tnil when fostered and encouraged as .they were liy the voluntary efforts of the teachers, 1% ho bad the futurejnterests' of the children at heart,- good results were bound to .follo iv.

div.head: Twenty Years' Work.
div.p: Twenty Years' Work.

As an illustration of the progress of the Bank for the last 20 years, A 474,000 had been ialdeci co the amount due to depositors, which was an increase of -59 per cent. on the figures of I 89!;. rhe number of accounts had increased by 3,0.1; and the turnover by 100 per cent. The special investment department still continued to be very popular, the public realising that they had a form of investment bearing u fair rate of interest, not quite so high, perhaps, as some of their friends in the industrial world had re- cently been offering, hut a perfectly :,ale one, knowing that the money was there when re- quired,- free from any fluctuations of the-money market, and always available: 'The resolution was carried.
Alderman SMETHMST moved tho adoption of the report of .the Committee of,Management and a vote of thanks to them for their services. Mr. SEGAR OWEN seconded, and the motion was carried.

The Rev. JOHN' YoNoE. moved the re-election of Mr. Long as .chairman and Mr, Jackson ',Holmes as vice-chairman. They. thanked Afr. 'Long for his -long and able services, but re- gretted he was not present that morning. They truSted, however, that his name would be asso- ciated with the Bank as long as he lived. in Mr. Jackson Holmes they. had an able vice-chair- man. (Hear, hear.) Mr. TINSLEY seconded, and the motion was heartily passed. • • • Mr. JACKSON. HOLMES replied on behalf of Mr. 'Long and himself. .The work of the Bank was a labour of love to him, and he hoped he Auld be permitted to serve it for some time. (ilear, hear.) .

Mr. William Skinner was re-elected treasurer and Mr. Arthur Bennett auditor. The follow- ing were also elected: Managers to join ~the trustees on the Committee of Management for the ensuing year, Messrs. J. S. Hill, L. R. Row- 3on, 5..11.. Smethurst, and the Revs. J. div.head: MARRIAGE PORTION.
div.p: A MARRIAGE PORTION.

Novelty is always more or less attractive, but o frequently the ,attraction vanishes when its newness has worn • off. • The Prudential • has introduced a distinct novelty in the way of life assnrance which increases in attractiveness each year. the .policy remains in force, and, in fact, has .a permanent value. 'Fhe policy enables the parent to mark the two most Important events in 'a child's life, viz., "the coming of age" and "marriage." An endowment assur- ance conies into force at the age of 21, and at marriage a cash payment is made, which varies with the length of time the policy has .been in force, and cannot fail to be substantial. This sum represents the full amount. of the bonuaes accrued to date of marriage. . The premiums are very moderate. Taking the example of a child aged one next birthday, a sum of ..t5ll on mar- riage at 23, and a further sum of £l3B :twenty years later, may be secured by an annual pay- ment . which barely exceeds I,!d. a day. In addition there is. the assurance of £lOO, together .with bonuses, at the .fixed and guaranteed rate of ,t 2 per annum, which will be • paid in the event of .death between the age of 21 and the maturity age. If the child fails to attain the age of 21, the whole of the premiums paid will be,re- turned, although a large sum may have already been received by way of bonus. if,enarriage has previously occurred. If the full term be sur- vived' the total amount received will be £lBB, and the total premiums paid cannot exceed ..£lO7 Is. 4d.

These figures Show what an excellent bargain is being o.Tfered by the Prudential. Full parti- culurs may be obtained from .Mr. Brecklehurst, at 69,. Sankey-street, the district office, of the e oinpau.

div.head: AMBULANCE WORK.
div.p: AMBULANCE WORK.
The Mayor, the Doctors and Others Raise Important Points.
LECTURE FEE PROBLEM.

Members of the _Warrington Corps of the St. John Ambulance Brigade were entertained to dinner by the superintendent and officers at Atkinson's Cafe on Saturday evening. An ex- cellent dinner was partaken of, and the post- prandial speeches •-• were of an encouraging nature. Dr. Adams (the corps surgeon) presided, and was supported by the Mayor (Councillor P. Peacock), the Deputy Mayor. Dr. Joseph), Mr. R. C. Parr, Mr. J. Fulton-Smith, the Chief Con- stable (Mr. Martin Nicholls), Dr. Law (divi- sional surgeon), Dr. Manson (divisional surgeon), Captain Waring (chief superintendent), Mr. T. S. Steel 'solicitor to the corps), Superintendent Baldry, First Officer IL T. Williams, Second Officer A. E. Spann. During the evening an en- joyable programme was contributed to by Mr. Dennett, Dr. Law, Mr. Williamson, and Mr. Price, whilst Mr. Grounds' sketches were highly amusing. Mr. Lofthouse was the accompanist. Letters of apology had been received, from Mr. A. IL Crosfield, Capt. Crosfield, Sir Gilbert Greenall, Bart., Mr. T. P. Bradshaw, M. Whitley, Major J. Geech, Mr. F. W. Monks, Mr. W. P. Rylands, Mr. J. Coxon, Mr. J. C. Parr, Mr. J. IL Clarke, and Deputy Commissioner Trimble.

div.head: FONDNESS FOR THE TOWN.
div.p: FONDNESS FOR THE TOWN.

On the. proposition of the CHAIRMAN the toast " The King"' was duly honoured, and at -a later stage Mr. T. S. STEEL proposed the toast of "The Town and Trade of Warrington." He said he always thought when he heard that toast pro- posed that it was proposing success to them- selves. When the town and trade were success- ful, it must naturally follow that they were successful with it. Warrington was a town which the more they lived in it, the fonder they got of it. (Hear, hear.) He had heard on several occasions of people coming to Warring- ton for the first time and saying "What a miser- able town it is," and it took some little time to get accustomed to it, but when they got accus- tomed to it, it was hard to drive them away from it-:--(hear, hear)—and that particularly ap- plied to Scotchmen. (Laughter.) There was one thing about the trade of Warrington, and that was, when other towns suffered from de- pression, Warrington did not suffer to the same extent. He thought a very great deal depended upon the way in which the muncipality admin- istered the law relating to the town, and he was very pleased to see the Mayor with them that night. (Hear, hear.) • They all congratulated him on his appointment, and wished him every success (luring his term of office. (Heat, hear.) He (Mr. Steel) was sure the Mayor would have the hearty support of the townspeople, and he thought that had already been shown during the short time he had occupied the Mayoral chair. At the present time there were many things occupying the attention of the Council. There was the question of the bridge—(laugh- ter)—which had been with them some time, and looked as if it would be with them:for some time to come. The Mayor had made a kind of prom- ise that the bridge would be completed during his term of office, and he (Mr. Steel) believed ' the Mayor would do all in his power to have the bridge completed by November next. • (Hear, hear, and. applause.) He noticed from the paper that his Worship had received a deputation with regard to the housing question, which Was a matter of great importance. They heard that rents in Warrington had increased, and houses were not being built with that rapidity which was shown some years ago. The population was increasing, and the number of weddings were going, on as years ago. It -naturally :followed. that something would have to be done, and when the Mayor .came to consider the particu- lars, he would bring to bear that intelligence and ability he possessed in seeing that something was done for the town in general. The Mayor was also in favour of the centralisation of the municipal buildings, which was a neces- sity. They hOped to see the matter settled in some :way or ,another,-.which would be satisfae- tOry to the great majority of townspeople. (Ap- plause.) He coupled with the toast the name of the Mayor, Councillor Peter Peacock.

div.head: MAYOR AND THE HOUSING QUES
div.p: THE MAYOR AND THE HOUSING QUES
TION.

-The Km% in reply, thanked the members for their -congratulations.. They were all proud of the ancient borough with its diversified trades, as a result of which they never' had that distiess- which was felt in other parts ,of the country so acutely. Each trade helped the other. He thought they could not separate the trade of Warrington from that great and noble organisa- tion,the St. John'Ambulance-Association, Which did so rimeh in alleviating- suffering in the various works and factories. With regard to the trade of Warrington, they • could compliment themselves on the fact that they had enjoyed prosperity for the last few years. He hoped the extensions going on amongst the works would continue to be necessary. Mr. Steel had men- tioned the housing question, which, to his mind, was one which must necessarily follow the ex- tension of trade. and works in the town, par- ticularly when something had come over the country which had put a stop to the building of houses. They remembered the time when hun- dreds of houses were being built per annum, but to-day they were building comparatively few. He had received •a deputation on the question, and Ale thought it only right and proper that the Deputy Mayor should be with him on that occasion, because he, the Mayor, knew Council- lor Dr. Joseph's heart was in the housing ques- tion in Warrington. Proper housing accommo- dation should be provided, and if the. builders did not step in, the town Must step in and answer the requirements. Dr. Joseph, Alder- man Evans and himself would have a -report of, " the empty houses in Warrington, • and whereas two Years ago there were 500 empty hiiuses, he did not think there were half that number to- day. A lot of people in Warrington had to live in the slums, and if they went to visit them, like Dr. Joseph and himself had done, they would find there we very little 0111413 re, %IPA sometimes nothing at all. Supposing the authorities closed those houses, where were those people to go? Suppose a row of municipal cot- tages were erected, those people would not want to go to them, and would not want the light of day to get to the houses. Where were they going to put the people? There was a dearth in property, which, he thought, was through busi- nesses which offered 12 or 20 per cent. He was always in favour of a steady four per cent.' People Who invested said they were going to have ,a flutter on a 20 to one chance, whether they -lost it in two years or not, they did not care. The men with the money -were not so ready in lending it to builders who controlled the erection of the houses, and therefore the builder must stop. •He did not blame the builder.. He knew several who had open fields, • and it was difficult for them to find the ground rent 'every year. They had to do that or go under. They had been asking for advances on property, and the investing public would not give money, and they were responsible for the shortage of .cottages. If the builders could not do it, the Town Council must take the matter •up, and build them themselves. (Hear, hear.) After referring to the Deputy Mayor as chair-. an of the Electricity and Tramways Committee, and saying that he had proposed they ,should spend ‘,215,000 on new extensions to increase the output, as well as getting introduced the over- lapping stages concession and getting free rides for the blind in Warrington, the Mayor said he would do his best to fill the office so ably held by his predecessor. (Hear, hear.) • He could not help wondering why other trades did not come to Warring,ton, notwithstanding the fact that they had :so many trades already. Warrington had the best railway connections and the finest waterways in the country, and a lot of land.. There was skilled ,lab-our better than any in England, and they could get any

div.head: WARRINGTON OBTAINS REVENGE.
div.p: WARRINGTON OBTAINS REVENGE.
Barrow Beaten at Wildersizoo After a Stirring, Hard Fought Klatch.
YOUNG PLAYS A VERY CLEVER GAME.
By 64 Scrum."

Revenge came like rare and refreshing fruit to Warrington. They pulled through an excit- ing, hard-fought game in a way that was most creditable, and by the 16 to 8 points defeat of Barrow found Ample satisfaction for the defeat in the first round Of the Lancashire' Cup earlier in the season. It was a great match, and Warrington deserved their victory, if only to emphasise the great improvement in their play. It was pleasant to watch the Warrington play. Every department worked well, and from back to front there was a much better understanding between the players than I :have seen this scason. The sequel to this was seen in the final score. Warrington started in a sensational manner. Cox charged down his initial kick, and it was as much as Morgan could do to kick dead to pre- vent the Warrington man from scoring. After this Barrow applied a bit of pressure. and this was relieved by a fine mark secured by Jolley. Young soon came into the picture and remained in it all the show. Ile brought off some clever, dashing runs, and if he had been backed up would have scored.

Daintith came away with a smart run, which resulted in him adding an unconverted try to the Warrington total. The "A" men thus ran out winners by 13 points to 5. This victory has enabled Warrington to strengthen their position at_the -top of the Com- bination table. They have now __played 12 matches, 11 of which they have won. They have scored 154 points against 49, .a.nd have a percentage of 91.66.

div.head: Tranter Opens With a Try.
div.p: Tranter Opens With a Try.

It was rather tantalising to see Warrington hovering on their opponents' line and yet not able to find an opening, which fact spoke well for the sturdy defence of the Barrovians. Tranter, who had been much in evidence with his footwork, got the ball from a scrum near the visitors' goal-line, dribbled a bit, then kicked strongly, followed up, and scored. Jolley kicked the goal with ease. After this Barrow put on a spurt and the War- rington goal had a narrow escape. Young, again with smart tactics, opened up the rood along which Ruddick dodged and ran until he crossed the line, well out, with a tricky earned try. Jolley was called upon to kick for goal at a difficult angle, and he just missed the uprights. Barrow next became prominent, and Doyle, with one of the dashes which characterised his game in the cup-tie, Outwitted Jolley and scored. Dobson added the additional points, and at half-time Warrington led by the narrow majority of 8 points to 5.
Other Eight Points Gained.

Bright as was the play in the first half, it was eclipsed by the stirring work in the second portion. Nicholas was first in evidence with a run, but he held on too long, and was grassed. Then came a sequence of tit-bits. Tranter, with a kick and follow-up caused Morgan to kick dead; Jolley nearly brought oil another of his sensational dropped goals, and to cap these mis- adventures, Chesters, taking up a dribble initiated by Fearnley, piloted the sphere over the line to score a neat try. Thomas struck the cross-bar with the kick. A few minutes after Thomas made amends for this inpreventable mishap by dropping a fine goal from near mid-field. Warrington, with a lead of eight points, were inclined to slacken, and Barrow took -advantage of it, with the result that Williams, possibly the speediest man on the Jield, dashed away and scored. _Robson kicked short. As time drew on Nicholas and Bradshaw indulged in a sharp bout of passing. Bradshaw, in final possession, dashed along the line, and scored a much deserved try. The kick failed, but at the close Warrington won by 2 goals 4 tries to 1 goal 2 tries.

Warrington's Marked Improvement. There was a marked improvement in the Warrington game. There was not so much passing as one could have liked, but perhaps this was occasioned by the admirable footwork. At times the game reminded one more of Asso- ciation than Rugby from the way the ball was manceuvred; and passed along from foot to foot. The forwards simply revelled in this style of play, and it had a great effect in securing the victory for Warrington. Fearnley was the chief figure in this style of play, and he was well backed up by Cox and Chesters. The others did also particularly well. Forward Warrington had an undoubted advantage in the loose, but the more weighty Barrow men were superior in the tight work. There was little difference between the two sets of back divisions.—keen half-backs, active, ambitious threequarters, and sturdy full-backs wore all of them. If anything the slight advan- tage in half-back play lay with Warrington.

div.head: Young's Fine Performance.
div.p: Young's Fine Performance.

Young, from the start till the close, gave an 1 excellent exhibition at stand-off. He gathered the ball smartly and used his head in the,plac- ing of it. On Saturday's play he easily stamped himself one of the smartest half-backs in the League. Nicholas worked better with his part- ner than he has yet done, and he got the hall out of the scrums more adroitly than he has done for some time. If the half-backs- can maintain this game they will materially assist Warrington in winning future matches. Everyone must welcome the improvement in Bradshaw. Ile has been under a cloud for some time, but now he has emerged I am hoping to see him score more triea like the one he secured towards the. close of the game. Dickenson was most conspicuous by his tackling tactics, and he in a goad.. measure was responsible for holding the speedy young threequarters of- Barrow in check.

div.head: Ruddick and Jolley.
div.p: Ruddick and Jolley.

Two outsts.nding men were Ruddick and Jolley. Ruddick played another particulady clever game, and proved that he has found .his proper position- in the threequarter line, al- though I still hold to the opinion that he, would be still more serviceable on the right wing. Tranter did fairly well, and he is the best partner Ruddick has yet had, but he was too miserly in his passes. Several times he ran into the nick when a short -pass out to Ruddick would have gained more. It is a fault that can be cured, and I think Tra.nter is capable of effecting a cure for this, probably unconscious, selfishness. ,Jolley was wherever he was wanted, and Only once did he make a slip. Good as Morgan was as the Barrow custodian, Jolley was easily his superior.

WARRINGTON "A" STILL WINNING. Pemberton Prove the Latest Victims. The Warrington "A " team keep running along the winning course, and Pemberton, play- on their own pitch, were the latest victims. The match proved keen and exciting, and it was Close- on the interval before Warrington man- aged to mark the score sheet. Waywell broke the ice with a prettily dropped goal. Soon after riarmer crossed the Pemberton line. Daintith inade no mistake with the kick and landed a 11, ice goal. Baker was next in the picture and he scored a pretty try, which was not converted. At the interval Warrington "A " led by 10 Points to nil. The second half witnessed much stronger play by Pemberton, who pressed for a time, during Which they secured a converted try. Later,

div.head: CHRISTMAS FARE. Oldham and Salford as Visitors.
div.p: THE CHRISTMAS FARE. Oldham and Salford as Visitors.

The bill of •fare for the Christmas holidays is one calculated to tempt the most jaded football appetite, and I am hopeful of seeing Warring- ton annex some useful League points out of the three matches. Two ought to be secured at Leigh on Christmas Day. On Boxing Da Y Old- ham visit Wilderspool. The Lancashire Cup- holders are playing an erratic game at present. and there is more than a sporting chance that 'Warrington will wipe out the defeat sustained at Watersbeddings on the 11th October. Sal- ford are due on Saturday, and I shall deal with that match in next week's isgoe. The "A" team have also an interesting pro- gramme, and ought to make their position at the had of the Combination even more secure. .Thil fixtures for the early part of the holidays 1,r3 : -
December 25.—Leigh v. Warrington—at Leigh. Warrington "A" v. Leigh "A"— at Wildersi)ool.
December 26.—WarringCon v. Oldham -- at Wilderspool. Oldham "A" v. Warrington "A" —at Oldham.
CAN WARRINGTON BEAT WIGAN? Great Match at Wllderspool To:day.

The most interesting match of thor season so far will be played at Wilderspool this afternoon, and there ought to be a record gate, for Wigan is always a great attraction. Last year War- rington were defeated by two points, the score being seven points to five in favour of 'Wigan. Can Warrington revenge this defeat to-day? I am hopeful that, they will. Since the Lanca- shire Cup final, Wigan, who-were runners-up, have been off their game, and now Warrington are nearly at the top of form I expect to see a victory, although I do not think many points will separate the sides. div.head: PICKS OUT OF THE SCRUM.
div.p: PICKS OUT OF THE SCRUM.

Pithy Pars About the N.U. Games. Wilderspoolians smiled. Revenge tasted very sweet. It was well-deserved also. . The previous disgrace in the Cup-tie was wiped out. Barrow did not expect defeat. In fact they laid odds on The prospect of again defeating Warrington with the cup-tie score. They came full of confidence. They returned much disappointed. It was "so unexpected, you know."

div.head: C CC Coe
div.p: C CC Coe

Cox gave the first sensation. It was clever the way he charged Down from the very kick-off. It was hard lines on Cox Not to have made a score from it. Tranter scored a very tricky try. Ruddick got also a try and He well merited that honour. The way the "little 'tin" dodged Delighted the Wilderspool onlookers. He is an adept at side-stepping. His opponents, of course, don't like it

0 Thomas dropped a lovely goal. One Manchester critic said he scored That from a mark—did he? Even Manchester critics make mistakes. Tranter also tried his foot at - An attempt to drop a goal. He didn't put enough pith Behind the ball to carry it goalwards. George Dickenson was a work glutton. The veteran simply revelled in Bringing down his opponents. As a defender he was great.

Bradshaw showed he can score. His dash up the line was good And his try was still better. Young Was the cutest half-back Seen on the field on Saturday. He has thoroughly got into the game. Young and Nicholas should now do Very well as half-back mates. The Wilderspool opinion was that Warrington have got a pair of half-backs Now in the process of making. Let us hope it will prove so.

div.head: BILLIARDS.

THE MATCH IN AID OF MRS. ARNIITAGE.
Ryland' Representatives Make Good Fight,
But Lose Heavily.

The match between a team representing Rylancis' Recreation and a team selected by Mr. T. Horrabin, in aid of the widow and family of the late Mr. J. Armitage, took place at Gorsey- lane on Monday night,• before a fairly large number of spectators. The team brought by Mr. Horrabin was one of the strongest that could possibly have been got together from this neighbourhood, and it was little wonder the home team won only three in twelve games, and that at the close they found themselves in a minority of 581. - _

The break of the evening was 45, unfinished, by G. Marshall, of the Senior Conservatives, who had also the second highest break of as., J. Leah, who did well to beat P. Ray, Junior Conservatives, ran out with 30 unfin- ished, and E. Walker, of Earlestown, who played a pretty game, bad a series of. nice runs, the chief of which totalled 27. Mr. R. V. div.head: SOME STIRRING WAIRMINGTOLI LEAGUE GAMES
div.p: SOME STIRRING WAIRMINGTOLI LEAGUE GAMES

Since the draw for the Cheshire Amateur Cup was made known, the most discussed topic has been the match between the local clubs, Stock- ton Heath and Latchford, the former gaining the benefit of the draw, and owing to the fact that the Heathens had defeated Lymm Ama- teurs, Northenden Amateurs and Oughtrington United, and the latter having defeated Latch- ford in the Senior Cup, all added flavour to the game. While the Latchford Club had been exempt from the first and second round, they managed to defeat Lymm at the second time of asking in the third round, and a better draw could not hardly have been anticiPated. The result was disappointing.
By 44 Lifiesman.”
opening half. Result: Crosfield's, one goal; Weston, none.

div.head: CHESHIRE AMATEUR CUP. Fourth Round. Sttckton Heath V. Latchford.
div.p: CHESHIRE AMATEUR CUP. Fourth Round. Sttckton Heath V. Latchford.

At the West Avenue ground. Teams :—Stock- ton Heath: Simcock ; Gosling and Woodward; Magill, Denny and Gifford; Antrobus, Lockhart, Jones, Smith and Taylor. Latchford: Kite; Robinson and "'aspen; Downs, Webb and Car- ter; Smith, P. Webb, Lees, Siddall and Fogg. Referee, W. S. Walker, Timperley. The first attack was initiated by Antrobus on the home right, who beat his opponent and raced along the touch line, centring finely, for Robinson to clear with a huge kick, which transferred play- into the home quarters. Gosling returned the leather, for Taylor to speed away on the left, only to be repulsed by the visitors' defence, and good combination by the visitors' front rank enabled them to get to the home goal, when P. Webb opened the score, Simcock having no chance with the shot. From a neat pass Taylor apin made an attack on the opposing goal, and centring beautifully, Smith sent in a fine drive, which caused Kite some trouble to clear. An- trobus was next prominent and made a grand effort to equalise, but Kite saved easily. The visitors, with the wind against them, managed to hold their own, and no further score was re- 'corded before the interval, which arrived with the score in their favour by one goal to none. The visitors, now having the aid of the wind, at once showed their superiority, and a second goal was recorded by Lees. This reverse ap- peared to be the knock-out blow for the Heathens, as from now the visitors had very much their own way. Haspell scored the third goal, and Smith a fourth. .Lees, the visitors' centre, was always on the look-out for chances that came his way, and he had the satisfaction of adding two more goals in quick succession. Further goals were added to the visitors' score by Haspell and Lees. Result: Latchford, eight goals; Stockton Heath, none.

div.head: WARRINGTON AND DISTRICT LEAGUE._ First Diviiiort.
div.p: WARRINGTON AND DISTRICT LEAGUE._ First Diviiiort.
Great Sankey v. DareSl3Ury.

Played on the Penketh .Reereation'Graund. Teams :—Great Sankey: Bond; Glover and Stephens; H. Ditchfield, Gardiner and Payne; Darlington, J. Ditchfield, Grainger, Poulter and Houghton, Daresbuu : Ravenscroft; Forster and de Prez; Houghton, Cash and Ryder; Cart- wright, F. Forster, L. Jones, J. Forster and Wil- kinson. H. Ditchfield was soon prominent with a good clearance, from which the home for- wards made a warm attack on the visitors' goal, when J. Ditchfield opened the score five min- utes from the start. Up to this point the visit- ors were playing a man short, and their reguiar custodian came on the field as the score was made. From the bentre kick play VMS confined to the visitors' half, and the efforts of the home team were repulsed time and again by the fine display of Ravenscroft in goal, and Forster and De Prez at full-back. Darlington, on the home right, made a fine centre, from which J. Ditch- field shot on the wrong side of the upright. The visitors' defence got relief and a visit was paid to the opposite end, when a final effort by F. Forster failed to equalise. From the goal kick , Grainger got possession and led the forwards splendidly, and J. Ditchfield passed to Darling- ton, who was well placed, and he notched a second point for the homesters. The interval found Sankey leading by two goals to nil. The visitors, ably led by Jones, made a spirited attack upon the home goal, where Stephens and Glover made some fine re. 'rue. Dhresbury were working hard, and fori d a couple of corners, which they failed to im, _eve upon. The ,home forwards now woke up and carried play into the visitors' quarters. Dar- lington centred right across the goalmouth, and Forster nipped in with a timely clearance. Ffoughton and Poulter, by good combination, again led an attack on the visitors' goals and Poulter gave Ravenscroft a warm handful, which he cleared. Forster and De Prez were rendering fine assistance. Houghton forced For- ster to concede a corner, which was well placed in goal, and after Ravenscroft had thrown, J. Ditchfield drove the ball in and registered the third goal. Time was called with the score: Great Sankey, three goals; Daresbury, nil.

Orford Barracks Weaver Refining Company. On the ground of the former. Teams : Orford Barracks: Tansley ; Topping and Stevens; Moody, Birkenhead and liughes; Roberts, Walker, Acton, Trafford and Spicer. Weaver Co. : -Mills; Woodward and H. Newton; W. Newton, Leicester and Beckett; Allcock, Evans, Johnson and Bean. The visitors had to play a man short. From the start the Soldiers monopolised the play, but were met by a. strong defence. After fifteen minsutes they were awarded a penalty kick, which was entrusted to Acton, but he failed to score. The home team held the visitors" in their half of the field, when Birkenhead sent in a rasping shot, which Mills failed to hold. From the centre kick the visit- ors made several strong attempts to break down the home defence, but failed in their efforts, and at half-time the Soldiers were leading by one goal to none. Weaver Refining now had the aid of the wind, and followed their opponents' example by mak- ing a strong attackion the home citadel. Tansley in goal was in grand form, and kept his charge from being captured. The visitors were handi- capped by being short of their full team, but they were successful in preventing the home team from increasing their score. Darkness stopped the game early, and then the Barracks team were leading by one goal to none.

div.head: Second Division.
div.p: Second Division.

Orford St. John's v. Warrington Excelsior. At Long-lane, Orford. it ,was soon evident that the game would be keenly contested. Milt- ward missed an easy chance of scoring by hesi- tating too long, but he made amends shortly after by scoriftg from a penalty kick for hands against Spencer. From a throw-in near the corner flag Redford hindled the bait in the dreaded area. Pritchard converting the kick. made the scores equal. The interval arrived with the score:. One goal each. The second portion started at a very hot pace, and some keen play was witnessed. The defence on both sides made a few mistakes owing to the excitement, but, always recovered, and on two or three occasions Forbes got•some long shots away in comfortable fashion, while at the other end Boyd was at fault in a similar manner, only. for Morris to prove himself equal to the emer- gency. The game ended in a draw of one goal each.
Bank Quay Recs. V. Fairfield.

At the Lovely-lane ground. The home for- wards laid siege on the visitors' goal, Bradshaw doing the needful. The home team again took up the attack, and the visitors' defence was severely tested. Eccleston scored the second goal for the Recs. Roberts miskicked and the 'ball went through his own goal, making the Recs.' score three up at half-time. Bradshaw passed to F,ccleston, who had not much difficulty in notching the fourth goal. Osborne reduced the lead with a good shot a few minutes before time. Result: Bank Quay Recs., four goals; Fairfield, one goal.

div.head: WIDNES AND DISTRICT ALLIANCE.
div.p: WIDNES AND DISTRICT ALLIANCE.

Farnwerth Institute v. Stockton Heath Reserve. At Farnworth. The opening exchanges were very -brisk and even, and each custodian was called upon to blear. Following a spell of mid- field play, a long, dropping shot was sent to- wards the visitors' goal and their defence was rushed, the ball being forced into the net. Even play followed, until Richardson sent out to Woodhead, the latter making a grand run on the right, centred at the right time, for Isherwood to nip in and equalise the score. The game was e'venly contested up to the interval, with the scores one goal each. The seeond half was keen, 'but without scor- ing. Result: One goal each.

div.head: WIDNES AND DISTRICT MINOR MEDAL COMPETITION. First Round—Replayed Tie. Widnes Albion v. Emmanuel Old Boys.
div.p: WIDNES AND DISTRICT MINOR MEDAL COMPETITION. First Round—Replayed Tie. Widnes Albion v. Emmanuel Old Boys.

The Old Boys visited Widnes to meet the Albion, who, had successfully laid a protest against them the previous Saturday. The Albion were at. once aggressive on the left wing, and they forced a corner, but Harrison headed away. The visitors then asserted themselves, and from a corner by Singleton, Hatton headed against the upright. There was now no stop- ping the visitors, and after Winstanley had smartly saved from Singleton and Wareham, Rigby tricked the defence and scored with a good shot, but Caldwell was adjudged offside. In. : Old Boys, nil; Albion, nil. The visitors proceeded to make headway, Ash- ton having hard lines with a fine shot. A fine passing movement between the Old Boys' for- wards resulted in the downhill of the Albion goal, Wareham smartly heading through from Rigby's centre. This success encouraged the visitors, and they attacked in combined order, Isherwood being fouled when becoming danger- ous. Hatton, with a strong shot, scored from the free kick. Rigby, after a fine run, transferred to Caldwell, who scored from short range, the Old Boys running out easy winners by three goals to nil.

div.head: FRIENDLY MATCHES.
div.p: FRIENDLY MATCHES.

Grappenhall St. Wilfrid's' v. Widnes Juniors. At Grappenhall. Ford and Watson were pro- minent with'a smart bit of combination on the right, from which a corner was forced. Grap- penhall were awarded a penalty for "hands," from which Watson scored. At this reverse the Juniors combined grandly, but the Grappenhall defence was sound, half-time arriving with Grappenhall leading 1-0. In the second half Grappenhall kept Widnes on the defence. Richards put in a shot, which, ,after being fisted out by the visiting goalkeeper, rebounded off one of the Widnes players into the net, the "Saints" running out winners by two goals to nil.
Emmanuel Institute v. Penketh Friends' ' School.

Played at Penketh. When the game had been in progress- ten minutes F. Berry opened the visitors' account with a shot that gave the home goalkeeper no Chance. From the kick-off Penketh dashed away, and after soMe fine combination between the home team,Palmer scored with a fast shot. Just before the interval Palmer scored his second goal after a melee in the goal- mouth. Half-time Penketh, two goals; Emmanuel, one. . .

Banner, who was playing a fine game, put in a huge kick, which enabled Roberts to send in a fine-centre, from which Oakes made no mis- take, thus putting- the visitors on level terms. The last ten minutes was played in semi-dark- ness, and during this the home team forced a corner, which was well placed, but Broadhurst managed to clear, although from a second shot the goalkeeper fisted the ball through his own goal. Penketh won by three goals to two.

MISCELLANEOUS ITEMS.
There was great joy in the Latchford camp over the result.
Webb proved too good for the " Heathen " forwards.

Denny was the best man on the Heath side. Lees scored four,' Haspell two, P. Webb and S. Smith one each. Stockton Heath forwards did not score at all. Fancy a full-back scoring twice. The gate receipts at Stockton Heath were close upon £4. The Medal Competition matches should be worth watching. The Warrington and District League have decided to run a Medal Competition. It is open to all junior clubs • within 10 miles of Market Gate, under the age of 21 years. Mr. R. G. Brandreth, Or!Ord, Warrington, will supply all information. In future they will play on a field adjoining the Recreation Ground at Hood-lane, where they will be pleased to welcome both old friends and new.

div.head: LATE DISTRICT NEWS.
div.p: LATE DISTRICT NEWS.
k ADGATE.

Cake and Apron Sale.—With the object of financially benefitting the Padgate District Nurses' Fund, a cake and apron sale was held in the Church of England Schools, Padgate, on Thursday evening, and was favoured by a good attendance. Dr. Bennett performed the open- ing ceremony. There was also a Christmas tree. Refreshments, &c., were served. It is expected that the effort has realised over A:l5.

div.head: HIGH LEGH.
div.p: HIGH LEGH.

Musical Success.—At a recent examination of the Incorporated Society ,of Musicians, held in Manchester for organ Playing, grade IV., ad- vanced, Mr. Herbert Atkinson, of High Legh, was successful in passing first class with honours. _

div.head: GREAT SANKEY.
div.p: GREAT SANKEY.

Girls' Friendly Society.—The members of this society held their annual social en Thursday night at St. Mary's Schools, when 120 persons were present. Choruses were rendered, and the solos were taken by Miss Blanes and Miss Clarke. Dancing was indulged in, and Miss Jessie .Cook accompanied. .The Rev. J. R. Jones presided.

Visit to a Sankey Fowlhouse.—At the War- rington County Petty Sessions, yesterday, before Mr. J. Rymer Young, Samuel Warburton, giv- ing an address at a Pig-hill lodging-house, was charged With breaking and entering the fowl- house of Mr. Thomas Cook, Holly House Farm, Great Sankey, and stealing four hens, value £l, between 18th and 19th December: Prisoner was seen at 5.30 yesterday morning by two con- stables of the Warrington Borough Police on the outskirts of the town. Prisoner pleaded guilty to taking the fowls, but denied that he broke into the fowlhouset---lle was remanded until Monday. .

div.head: PENKETH.
div.p: PENKETH.

Council School: Annual Concert. Dr. Murray on Thursday presided over the concert organised annually by the teaching staff of the Penketh Council School, and it must have been very gratifying to see the spacious schoolroom so crowded. The opening item "Blow, soft winds," was sweetly sung by the scholars, and afterwards a character sketch, "The Green- grocer," was portraked by Joseph Baekhouse, assisted by Fred. Hobson, Willie Roberts, Eva Glassey, Ethel Fisher and Irene Hatton (cus- tomers). The "Lost chord" was well ren- dered by Gladys Jones, and the Morris dancers played an important part in the programme. Mary Cunliffe proved to be an ideal Gipsy Queen, and her subjects also, took their parts admirably. The " Suffragettes " was much en- joyed by the audience, and Gladys Jones, as the leading suffragette, won universal ,favour. Bessie and Eric Hatton played a violin and pianoforte duet, and were applauded for their efforts. "Barney O'llea " was danced in cos- tume by Lily Bailey, Doris Baker, Ethel David- son, Hilda Bowyer, Annie Knowles, Gladys Jones, Doris Wing,' and Nellie Thomas; and "Grow, little mushroom," a beautiful song, fol- lowed next, by Amy Carrington, Beatie Goulden, Gladys Bond, Doris Heath, Elsie Rogers; Hilda Jones, Emily Teat and Isabel Rontledge, which earned for them loud ap- plause. Much amusement was created by the sketch, "The three tramps," the characters being taken by Reginald Fisher, 'Reginald Lox- ley and Isaac Manes; and " Good-u ight " was the terminating item, which was effectively ren- dered. The Chairman, in a few remarks, said it had given him great pleasure to witness the fine performance, and this was suitably re- sponded to by Mr. D. R. Griffiths (headmaster), who, on behalf of himself, Mrs. T. Bell, and the staff, said the training had been a labour of rove.

div.head: PRIORY sCHuOL.
div.p: THE PRIORY sCHuOL.
Deputy-Mayor Presents Prizes.

The prize, distribution in connection with the Priory 'School took place on Wednesday even- ing. Councillor Dr. Joseph presided, and at an interval presented the prizes. He spoke in eulogistic terms of the value of education given at private schools, which, he stated, received no help from public sources. The prize list was as follows: Dolly Hughes, lower school conduct; Marjory Landon, Wilmett Fox and Connie Hughes, 'kindergarten; Kath- leen Byerley, general proficiency; R,eggie Cor- bett, attendance; Marie Byerley, middle school conduct, drawing certificate Division I. (pass); Sybil Tinnion, music, drawing certificate Divi- sion I. (pass); Hector Nicholls, attendance, honours, drawing certificate Division I.; Jessie Ferguson, Form 11. prize, honours, drawing certificate Division I.; Vera Nicholls, Form 111. prize; Alice Wilkinson, Form IV. prize, two honours, drawing certificates Divisions I. and II.; Cissie Allen, needlework; Isabel Ferguson, attendance, Form V. prize, certificate for music, Associated Board of the R.A.M.. and R.C.M.; ,Clarice Ball, Form VI. prize, Oxford Local -Senior certificate; Dolly Percival, upper school conduct prize (awarded on vote of girls them- tielves), drawing, and drawing certificate R.D.S. Division V.; Elsie Armstrong, special examina- tion ; Gertrude Hunt, music certificate Associ- ated Board of R.A.M. and R.C.M., two honours drawing certificates Division I and II.; Lilian Forrest, honours drawing certificate Division 1., honours certificate Division III.; Xvy Price, two hon Ours drawing certificates Division I. and II.; Kathleen Hollingworth, honours drawing certificate Division - II.; Edith Roger, one honours , drawing certificate; Doris Kerfoot, music certificate Associated Board of R.A.M. and R.C.M., primary, Division 1., drawing cer- tificate Division II.; Hermie Mason, two honours drawing certificates Division IIL and, IV.; Annie Armstrong, one honours drawing certifi- cate Division 111., one pass certificate Divi- sion IV.; Muriel Acton, one honours drawing certificate, R.D.S., Division V.

In her report the Head Mistress, Miss Dring, said the number of scholars had increased. Probably the most notable success of the last two years was that of, Elsie Armstrong, who passed the Oxford Senior-Local with first-class honours and distinction in English literature. In July Clarice Ball also passed the Senior Local.

div.head: Entertainment.
div.p: The Entertainment.

• The entertainment which followed was most successful, the children having been splendidly trained by Miss Woodward and. Miss Price. The bright- singing and dancing of the girls, together with the sparkling music, gave great pleasure to the crowded audience. The action songs were very effective, and, indeed, the whole programme was an excellent one, "The Two Gentlemen of Verona" and " The Enchanted Glen" being items worthy of special commen- dation. Those who contributed to the evening's enjoyment were: The Misses Phyllis Ellis and Gwen. Bennett, Katie Price. D. Fletcher, D. Percival, H. Houghton, E. Arm- strong, A. Armstrong, Ivy Price, Alice Wilkin- son, Vera Nicholls, Sybil Tinnion. Gerty Hunt. Marie Byerle3r, Kathleen Hollingworth. Isabel Ferguson, Mary Allen, Edith IRoger, Kathleen 13yerley, Cissie Allen, Lilian Forrest, Doris Ker- foot, Jessie Ferguson, Joan Anderson, Dolly and Connie Hughes, Marjorie Landon, Wilmett Fox, Eveline Parfitt and Eva Denham.

div.head: SECONDARY SCHOOL.
div.p: SECONDARY SCHOOL.
The Old Students' Re-Union.

The annual reunion of the old students of the Secondary School took place on Thursiay even- ing in the Gymnasium. The old building was tastefully decorated, and when the dancing ivas going on the pretty dresses of the ladies Liade the ordinarily business-looking place seem quite like a fairy scene. The first part cd the evening was given up to whist, and everybody -cemaql to play, in real earnest, for was there not a pri3:4' (or two), for the highest number of tricks? When .the. number were taken the fortunate ones to ,receive these tokens were Miss May Downing, first prize; Mrs. Baxter, second prize; and for the gentlemen Mr. Ronald Leigh car,. off the. first trophy and Mr. Price the second.

Mr. Robson made a short speech and said he was pleased ta see that there were old students m!embled there Who had attended the school when it was first opened, and also there were students from every year onwards to the pre- sent time.

Then supper was served, and, afterwards the floor was cleared for dancing: The M.C.'s were Messrs. Baxter, Broome and Furness, who 'were. very energetic. .in their duties. As the early hours of morning came in, the dancing finished,. and everybody went home feeling that the even- ing had been a huge success, and no doubt next year the numbers will grow to such an extent that the committee will have to engage the Parr Hall, in Order to accommodate the old students froth the Secondary School.

COUNTY BOROUGH OF WARRINGTON. ELECTRICITY DEPARTMENT. The Electricity and Tramways Committee of the County Borough of Warrington invite Tenders for WELDLESS STEEL PIPES for feeding Boilers. Specification and Form of Tender can be obteined from the undersigned on payment of One Guinea, which will be returned on receipt of a bona-fide tender. Five Shillings will be charged for extra copies of specification. Tenders, addressed to the Chairman of the Electricity and Tramways Committee, Town Hall, Warrington, must/be sealed with wax and endorsed Tender for Steel Pipes," and delivered not later than 12 o'clock noon on Wednesday, January 7th, 1914. The lowest or any tender will not necessarily be accepted. F. V. L. MATHIAS, M.1.E.E., Borough Electrical & Tramways Engineer. Howley, Warrington. COUNTY BOROUGH OF WARRINGTON. . EDUCATION COMMITTEE. TO BUILDERS AND CONTRACTORS. The SITES and BUILDINGS COMMITTEE is prepared to receive TENDERS for the ERECTION of a PUBLIC ELEMENTARY I SCHOOL, to be known as the Oakwood Avenue Council School. Bills of Quantities and Instructions to Builders and Contractors may be obtained on and after the 22nd December from the Educa- tion Office on payment of One Guinea, which will be returned upon the receipt of a bona-fide tender. The Tenders must he delivered at the Educa- tion Office in the envelope supplied (which must be securely sealed with wax) by not later than 12 o'clock noon on Friday, the 16th 'January, 1914. The Committee does not bind itself to accept the lowest or any Tender. J. MOORE MURRAY, M.Sc., Secretary and Director. Education Office, Warrington, 10th December, 1913.

CROSS COUNTRY. Warrington A.C. had a good muster racing for •points over a 61 mile trail, laid by F. Price and H. Pugh. The pace was good, and Holbrook was chased home by Hanson and Vose, closely fol- lowed by E. Scott and Parsonage. Including Saturday's result, the points competitions now stand :—Senior: J. Hanson, 19; H. Holbrook, 19; C. Vose, 16; E. Scott, 14; J. Parsonage, 12; F. Antrobus, 10; and J. Hayes, 5. Intermediate: E. Scott, 40; J. Hayes, 30; A. Potts, 24; S. Grounds, 20. Novice: A. 'Pats, 27; A. Inman, El; H. Leach, 21; J. Scott, 17; A. Hazelhurst, 13; T. Howliston, 9; and E. Gibson, 7. Coming Fixtures. To-day the married v. single run over the prospective course for the annual handicap, which will, as usual, be run off on Christmas morning, when members are requested. to turn up in good time; the rlimit man starts at 10.10 a.m., and laggards will be left, as the idea is to finish the race before the local football math starts. All athletes residing within 10 miles of War- rington, who have not won a prize of any kind for running, are requested to attend a meeting at the local club's pavilion, near the Football Ground, at 2.15 p.m. to-day.

Warrington Workingmen's Association. • N.A. CENTRE. PRIZE LIST CORRECTION. In the pike prizes: 1, 11. Mounfield ; 2, R. Clare. Trout: 1, H. Brittain; 2, J. Chadwick. GENERAL MEETING. The date arranged for the amalgamated general meeting is January sth. Notices will be put up in all club houses giving particulars. LETTER FROM THE STATES. Many thanks to P. Tully for his letter from the States, published in last week's "Examiner." We are always pleased to hear from our old members across the seas. Perhaps they will send us a few notes telling us how they find angling out there, as it would be interesting reading to their old friends. P.T.'s letter was read before the Warrington Committee, and they all send him their compliments and wish him and his family a merry Christmas and a pros-. perous New Year. A.S. DELEGATES' REPORT. This report, owing to Christmas pressure on our space, is held over till next week'.
